name: Intuitive Machines, Inc.
industry: Aerospace and Defense / Space Systems / Lunar Logistics
title: Intuitive Machines — the first private moon-landing company that now wants to be a space prime
subtitle: From Steve Altemus's NASA JSC engineering office to a $4.82B NASA contract ceiling, an $800M Lanteris acquisition, and a 2026 outlook of $900M-$1B revenue — what does it take to industrialise lunar logistics?
abstract: Intuitive Machines, Inc. (LUNR, NASDAQ) is the Houston-based lunar-logistics and broader space systems company co-founded in 2013 by Stephen Altemus (President and CEO, ex-NASA JSC Deputy Director who led the Columbia Reconstruction effort) and Dr. Kamal Ghaffarian (Chairman, co-founder of Stinger Ghaffarian Technologies, Axiom Space, X Energy, Quantum Space, and PTX). The company de-SPAC'd in February 2023 via Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. and began commercial operations as the first private company to successfully land a spacecraft on the Moon's surface (IM-1 'Odysseus,' February 22 2024). FY2025 produced Q4 revenue of $44.8M and full-year revenue in the $250-300M range, against a 19% Q4 gross margin and an FY2026 revenue outlook of $900M to $1 billion with positive Adjusted EBITDA. The transformational corporate event of the year was the announced $800 million acquisition of Lanteris Space Systems ($450M cash, $350M stock, expected close Q1 2026) — bringing in Boeing satellite systems veteran Chris Johnson as President of the acquired business and lifting total backlog to $943 million. The Lanteris deal explicitly transforms Intuitive Machines from a pure-play lunar delivery specialist into a full space prime contractor with satellite, lunar logistics, and broader space-systems product lines. The NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) ceiling contract is $4.82 billion with $150M guaranteed near-term, and a separate $180.4M CLPS task order announced for IM-5 will deliver seven science and technology payloads to the Lunar South Pole using the larger cargo-class Nova-D lander. The board (Class I: Liquori retired LtGen US Space Force, Masson ex-Raytheon/Naval Aviator CFO; Class II: Blitzer Kingstown Capital founder + USA Rare Earth chair, Seligman ex-Sony GC and President + OpenAI director + Harvard Law magna; Class III: Ghaffarian chairman, Altemus CEO) is unusually deep on national security and aerospace credentials. The investment proposition compresses NASA-procurement cycle execution, lunar-mission technical risk (IM-1 partial success despite landing; IM-2 also delivered to lunar surface), Lanteris integration, and the secular thesis that lunar logistics becomes a sustainable commercial market through the 2030s — with the SpaceX / Blue Origin / Astrobotic competitive set at varying stages of overlap.
